newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian bonds end higher but issue could weigh.
newsitem.headline: Austrian bonds end higher but issue could weigh.

text.p: 1630 GMT - Austrian bonds advanced on Monday, helped by the resolution of a domestic political crisis over the privatisation of bank Creditanstalt and a slight recovery in U.S. Treasuries.
Traders were downbeat about news Austria planned to issue a 10-year, 15 billion schillings bond on Tuesday, however, saying the market would have preferred a six to eight-year bond.
* Latest 10 year benchmark 5.875 pct bond maturing July 2006 up 30 bps at 100.30 to yield 5.83 (5.87) pct in bourse trade, quoted post-market at 100.29/37 to yield 5.83/82.
* At the near end, five-year 5.50 percent bond maturing March 2001 up 25 bps at 103.65 to yield 4.57 (4.63) percent in bourse trade, quoted post-market at 103.73/81 to yield 4.55/53 percent.
* AGB future up 77 bps at 107.55 on turnover of 265 lots.
* 10-year spread to German bunds up five at one bp, five-year spread down one at 13 bps.
* Money market rates steady with three-month VIBOR steady at 3.350 and overnight money at 3.15/3.40. -- Vienna newsroom, +431 53112 257
